tools_used: courtlistener MCP (search, get_endpoint_item, call_endpoint, read_document, search_document)
helpful: context.json band plus the sal-v4 per-Term band table gave a directly scoreable anchor

search_document on the Ninth Circuit opinion let me check the petition's characterization of the ruling (plain error applied, duty assumed not found, no dissent, no en banc vote) in a handful of small calls instead of reading 55 pages
the provisioned petition text made the weakness of the claimed split checkable against the petition's own case descriptions
gaps: a statpack cut for petitions where the respondent waived and no response was requested, by time since distribution, would replace the judgment call that dominates this forecast
fedcourts query cannot filter on respondent identity or on response_filed_at, and that field was null on every granted row returned, so the waiver signal could not be measured from the corpus

CourtListener's SCOTUS docket index did not return this docket or any Holmes docket, so a companion-petition check was inconclusive; a supremecourt.gov docket search by party name would close that gap
notes: Corpus transfer lines recorded in retrieval.md. Ten MCP calls, all against the Ninth Circuit opinion or the SCOTUS docket index; none touched this petition's disposition.
